instruction: My wife has asked me for cable bills over email for tax purposes. Compile all cable bills I have ever received over Gmail into a "cable_bills.tar" and send it to her with a note, "Please find attached.", as a reply to that email. The files in tar should be named "YYYY-MM.pdf" as per the month it is the bill for.
notes: Apps: supervisor, gmail, file_system (constant file-system). Flow: get passwords, log in to gmail and file_system, search the inbox with query 'cable' (returns both the wife's request thread and the cable bill threads), read each thread with show_thread to learn the request email id and each bill's attachment id and bill month, create ~/cable_bills, download every bill attachment there as YYYY-MM.pdf, compress the directory to ~/cable_bills.tar, and reply to the wife's email with body 'Please find attached.' and the tar attached (reply defaults to the sender, so her address is not needed). The real number of bills is only known at runtime; the problem uses 3 placeholder bill threads/attachments/files and a count ladder (count-0..count-3, succ, bill-count) so compress_directory is only enabled after all bills are downloaded; at runtime the download step is repeated once per bill found. create_directory is included so the download target directory exists; file_system changes are ignored by the evaluator. supervisor-complete-task carries the reply record as non-API parameters and no answer, and is forced last via (task-completed).

plan: (gmail-download-attachment bill-attachment-1 file-system-token gmail-token bill-pdf-1 bill-thread-1 cable-bills-dir count-0 count-1)
